entities.name: Infante Ferdinand, Duke of Viseu
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Infante Ferdinand, born on November 17, 1433, was a pivotal figure in the Portuguese royal house of Aviz during the burgeoning Age of Discovery, serving as the first Duke of Beja from 1453 and the second Duke of Viseu from 1460. As the third son of King Edward of Portugal and Eleanor of Aragon, Ferdinand occupied a significant position within the dynastic succession, especially before the birth of his nephew, John II. His life was deeply intertwined with the geopolitical ambitions of Portugal, particularly its expansion into North Africa and the Atlantic, and he was a prominent landholder whose titles reflected the growing power and wealth of the Portuguese monarchy in the mid-15th century.

Ferdinand's career saw him participate directly in the Portuguese military expeditions against Moorish strongholds. Notably, he accompanied his elder brother, King Afonso V, in the successful conquest of Alcácer-Ceguer (Ksar es-Seghir) in 1458, a strategic port on the Moroccan coast. This campaign was a continuation of Portugal's Reconquista efforts and its broader imperial designs. His ducal titles, particularly Viseu, were inherited from his influential uncle, Infante Henry the Navigator, whose legacy of exploration and maritime endeavor Ferdinand was expected to uphold and perpetuate through his own administration of their associated revenues and territories.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Infante Ferdinand's significance stems from his direct lineage to Manuel I, whose reign profoundly shaped Portugal's global empire and world trade routes. His role in consolidating ducal power also contributed to the stability and wealth of the Portuguese crown during a period of intense expansion.
